text: In nineteen twenty-five, a man sold the Eiffel Tower. Then he came back, and tried to sell it again.
sub: In 1925, a man sold the Eiffel Tower. Then he came back, and tried to sell it again.
asr: In 1925, a man sold the Eiffel Tower, then he came back and tried to sell it again.

text: His name was Victor Lustig. And he never owned a single bolt of it.
sub: His name was Victor Lustig. And he never owned a single bolt of it.

text: As the story goes, it began with a newspaper. The tower was rusting, and repairs were expensive.
sub: As the story goes, it began with a newspaper. The tower was rusting, and repairs were expensive.

text: Victor Lustig saw an opportunity. He printed official-looking letters, and invited scrap dealers to a secret meeting, in a grand Paris hotel.
sub: Lustig saw an opportunity. He printed official-looking letters, and invited scrap dealers to a secret meeting, in a grand Paris hotel.

text: Posing as a government official, he said the city would sell the tower for scrap. Seven thousand tons of iron. Top secret.

asr: Posing as a government official, he said the city would sell the tower for scrap – 7,000 tons of iron, top secret.

text: One dealer, Ahndray Pwasson, wanted it badly. He was new in Paris, and wanted to be someone.
sub: One dealer, André Poisson, wanted it badly. He was new in Paris, and wanted to be someone.
asr: One dealer, Andre P. Wassen, wanted it badly. He was new in Paris and wanted to be someone.

text: But he had doubts. Why so secret? Why so fast?

text: So he confessed. Officials were badly paid. He wanted a bribe.

text: And that convinced him. Only a real official would ask for a bribe.

text: Pwasson paid for the tower, and the bribe. Lustig took the money, and left the country.

text: And Pwasson? He was too embarrassed to tell the police.

text: So Lustig came back, and tried to sell it again. This time, someone called the police. He slipped away.

text: Years later, he was caught in America, for printing fake money.

text: The tower is still standing. Still not for sale.
